channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz in seven days for sanctions relief and $12 billion
item.description: Iran has officially proposed a seven-day plan to the US via intermediaries to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that normal shipping could resume within seven days if conditions are met, including cessation of hostilities and lifting of naval blockades.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva discusses Tashkent International Financial Center launch with BlackRock
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan and manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center, met with BlackRock leadership in New York. They discussed the launch of the center, planned for 2027, with BlackRock assisting in its concept and structure development.

item.title: Pakistan PM Tells UN Afghanistan's Soil Used Against Pakistan
item.description: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stated at the UN General Assembly that Afghanistan's territory is being used for attacks against Pakistan by groups like TTP and BLA. He urged the Taliban to fulfill international commitments and take verifiable steps to prevent such usage. Sharif also highlighted terrorism as a major threat to global peace.

item.title: Uzbekistan power outage causes Kazakhstan electricity disruption
item.description: A malfunction in Uzbekistan led to a power outage in Kazakhstan. Compensation will be paid if electricity supply disruptions are not resolved on time. Separately, a prosecutor's assistant was arrested for bribery in Tashkent region, and cooler weather is expected in Uzbekistan over the weekend. Uzbekistan also defeated the USA in chess.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Accused of Funding ISIS Extradited to the US from Georgia
item.description: Dovud Ansoriy, an Uzbek citizen and US national, has been extradited to the United States from Georgia. He is accused of leading a secret network that financed ISIS and the Al-Nusra Front. Ansoriy had been sought for 10 years before his arrest.

item.title: Kazakh President Sends Condolences to Families of Soldiers Lost in Mangystau Incident
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has sent condolences to the families of military personnel who died during naval exercises in the Mangystau region. Heavy weather conditions led to 17 servicemen being swept into the sea, resulting in 14 confirmed deaths. An investigation is underway, and the families will receive necessary assistance.

item.title: Families of Soldiers Killed in Mangystau Receive Condolence Telegrams from President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent personal condolence telegrams to the families of soldiers who died during exercises in the Mangystau region. He assured them of necessary assistance and promised strict punishment for those responsible for the tragedy.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Healthcare Reforms: Transparency, Trust, and Anti-Corruption
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing healthcare reforms to enhance transparency, accountability, and combat corruption under President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Deputy Health Minister Jaloliddin Asamutdinov highlighted that improved quality of medical services and fair access to treatment are key outcomes for patients.

item.title: Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia military chiefs to meet in Riyadh
item.description: Military leaders from Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia will convene in Riyadh for a defense pact meeting. This gathering occurs amidst increased Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The meeting aims to discuss support for the Kingdom under a joint defense agreement signed last month, which mandates mutual defense if any member is attacked.

item.title: China explains J-10 fighter jet deliveries to Uzbekistan
item.description: China's Ministry of National Defense stated that deliveries of J-10CE fighter jets to Uzbekistan are not directed against any third country. A spokesperson affirmed that military cooperation between China and Uzbekistan is developing amicably and aligns with international law and practice. Uzbekistan became the second foreign customer for this aircraft model after Pakistan.

item.title: Third Survivor of Caspian Sea Military Exercise Incident Under Medical Observation
item.description: The Ministry of Defense reported that the third surviving serviceman from the Caspian Sea military exercise incident is under medical observation and is in good condition. Nikita Udlov, from West Kazakhstan region, is one of the survivors, alongside Beket Kuandyk and Akzhol Temirkhan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Electricity Imports from Four Nations for Winter
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has finalized agreements to import electricity from Kazakhstan, Russia, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan for the upcoming autumn-winter period. The energy ministry reports that 85% of equipment repairs are complete, ensuring sufficient supply. Officials urged public conservation to avoid potential outages.

item.title: Flowers Laid at Kazakhstan's Embassy and Consulates in Russia Following Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: Residents in six Russian cities are laying flowers at Kazakh diplomatic missions to mourn military personnel lost at sea. Three soldiers were rescued, while 14 perished during exercises in the Caspian Sea due to sudden weather deterioration. Condolences are being expressed.

item.title: Three Arrested in Tashkent for Attempting to Enroll Student with Fake Documents
item.description: Three individuals, including an inspector-psychologist from the Yakkasaroy district police department, were detained in Tashkent for allegedly taking $7,500 to enroll a student in the third year of a private university using forged documents.

item.title: Military Personnel Who Died in Mangystau to Be Nominated for State Awards
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev sent condolences to the families of military personnel who died during exercises in Mangystau. The state media reported that the deceased will be nominated for state awards, and those responsible for the incident will face severe punishment.

item.title: Uzbekistan to improve agricultural subsidies and insurance systems with result-based approach
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed proposals to enhance agricultural subsidies and insurance. The government aims to shift from a 'fund allocation' model to a 'results-based subsidy' model starting next year. Key criteria will include yield, water and energy savings, and output per resource unit, tracked via digital systems without human intervention.

item.title: Logistics complex worth 3 billion soms to be built in Kyzyl-Kiya
item.description: Construction of a transport and trade logistics complex valued at approximately 3 billion soms has begun in Kyzyl-Kiya. The facility will be located on a 13-hectare site and is being developed under a public-private partnership. The project aims to create over 3,000 jobs and boost trade and logistics services.

item.title: Pakistani Drones Patrol Khost and Paktia Provinces Amid Taliban Fire
item.description: Pakistani drones have been observed patrolling over Afghanistan's Khost and Paktia provinces since Friday morning. Taliban fighters reportedly fired heavy weapons at the drones. This follows Pakistani airstrikes on Kandahar, Khost, and Paktia provinces earlier in the week, which Pakistan claims targeted militant camps.

item.title: World Leaders Send Condolences to Tokayev After Caspian Sea Tragedy
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has received condolence messages from foreign leaders and international organizations following the deaths of servicemen during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Leaders expressed solidarity with Kazakhstan and offered sympathy to the families of the deceased.

item.title: Macron, Aliyev, and Other Leaders Offer Condolences for Caspian Sea Tragedy
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has received condolence messages from numerous world leaders, including Presidents Macron of France and Aliyev of Azerbaijan, following the deaths of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea naval exercises. The leaders expressed solidarity with Kazakhstan and offered sympathy to the families of the deceased.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Fatal Military Exercise Incident, Declares National Day of Mourning
item.description: A tragic incident during military exercises in the Mangystau region resulted in the deaths of 14 servicemen. The government has launched an investigation, with a governmental commission working on-site. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev declared September 25 a national day of mourning.

item.title: International Leaders Offer Condolences for Kazakh Servicemen's Deaths
item.description: Heads of foreign states and international organizations have sent condolence messages to Kazakhstan's President regarding the deaths of servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. Leaders from Tajikistan, Azerbaijan, Belarus, France, Serbia, Vietnam, Armenia, and Tatarstan expressed their sorrow.

item.title: Kazakh sailors die during Caspian naval exercise; five officers arrested
item.description: Fourteen Kazakh sailors drowned during maritime drills on the Caspian Sea due to weather conditions and strong waves. Three sailors were rescued, and 12 bodies were recovered. Five officers, including the deputy commander-in-chief, have been arrested as a criminal investigation is opened. The president declared a national day of mourning.

item.title: China and Kazakhstan deepen economic ties with IT/AI and investment forum
item.description: A Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum in Almaty has resulted in agreements boosting Chinese influence in automaking, green energy, IT/AI, and fertilizer production. An investment fund for promising startups will be established at the Astana International Financial Center. China is Kazakhstan's main trading partner, with over 260 collaborative projects valued at over $62 billion.

item.title: Five killed in Russian drone attack on Kyiv, targeting office buildings and warehouses
item.description: Five people were killed in a Russian drone attack on Kyiv. The drones targeted office buildings, a McDonald's warehouse, and other civilian structures. Further details are available on daryo.uz.

item.title: Civil activist Sanjar Bokayev's trial postponed to October 16
item.description: The trial of civil activist Sanjar Bokayev, originally scheduled for September 28, has been postponed to October 16. The postponement is due to his transfer to Astana. Bokayev has been in custody since March 18, suspected of spreading false information online about illegal logging and theft.

item.title: Presidential Election Scheduled for January 27, 2027, in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election is set for January 27, 2027. The Central Election Commission has called on voters, candidates, parties, and media regarding the upcoming vote. Citizens aged 18 and over must complete biometric registration to be included in voter lists. Those abroad can vote via diplomatic missions. Candidates must be at least 35, fluent in the state language, and have resided in the country for 15 years.

item.title: Uzbekistan Moving Beyond Poverty Towards Middle-Income Status, World Bank Reports
item.description: Uzbekistan is transitioning from poverty to middle-income status, with poverty levels dropping to 5.8% and the middle class growing to 72%, according to a new World Bank report. The report, prepared with Uzbek ministries, highlights achievements and risks. The World Bank recommends ensuring all citizens have access to skills, services, and opportunities for a secure life, regardless of location, gender, or social background.

item.title: Fourteen Military Servicemen Die During Caspian Sea Exercise, Ministry of Defense Confirms
item.description: The Ministry of Defense has officially announced the deaths of 14 military personnel during an exercise in the Caspian Sea. Social media has seen an outpouring of condolences for the deceased servicemen, including Madikhan Azamat Bolatbekuly and Tolegen Akylbek Kabenuly. Support will be provided to the families.

item.title: Kazakhstan establishes diplomatic ties with Central African Republic, discusses UN agenda
item.description: Kazakhstan and the Central African Republic have established diplomatic relations, with a joint communique signed in New York during the UN General Assembly. Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi also met with international counterparts to discuss bilateral relations and global issues.

item.title: Kazakh President Did Not Visit Aktau After Soldiers Died in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: The death toll of soldiers in the Caspian Sea incident has reached 14. Authorities have detained at least five individuals in connection with the incident where soldiers were reportedly made to jump into the water on a windy day. President Tokayev did not visit Aktau.

item.title: Kazakh, Russian Foreign Ministers discuss strategic partnership at UN
item.description: Kazakh Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met in New York during the UN General Assembly to discuss bilateral cooperation and regional and international issues. Both sides reaffirmed their interest in strengthening the strategic partnership between Kazakhstan and Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President meets with Chinese cultural delegation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received a delegation from the China International Cultural Communication Center and JDB Group. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations, cultural ties, and cooperation in infrastructure, investment, and green industry. Priority areas for JDB Group in Uzbekistan include urban, transport, and industrial infrastructure development.

item.title: Almaty Airport offers free VIP services for families of deceased servicemen
item.description: Almaty Airport is providing complimentary VIP escort services for immediate relatives of servicemen killed or surviving during Caspian Sea exercises. The offer, valid until October 3, 2026, also extends to the surviving military personnel. Proof of kinship is required for relatives.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Navy Deputy Commander Identified Amid Arrest Reports
item.description: First Deputy Commander of the Kazakh Naval Forces, Daniyar Khairushev, has been identified. State media reported that Khairushev, a career serviceman, previously commanded a naval base in Aktau and participated in international exercises. His recent roles focused on combat readiness and training.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Online Police Recruitment Platform for Equal Access
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has launched Qyzmet-Police.kz, a digital platform for online police recruitment. The system automates applications, eliminating queues and paperwork, and allows candidates to track their status. It ensures equal access regardless of location or connections.

item.title: Kazakhstan to support families of servicemen lost at sea
item.description: Kazakhstan has completed fundraising for families of servicemen who died during Caspian Sea exercises. A special fund has been established for transparent distribution of aid. The government will fulfill all its obligations to support the families, assigning specialists to assist each one.

item.title: Kazakh Vice-Premier Promises Prompt Payments to Families of Caspian Sea Military Fatalities
item.description: Kazakh Vice-Premier Kanat Bozumbayev assured that families of sailors who died during Caspian Sea exercises will receive payments without delay. The state will fully cover all obligations, with responsible specialists assigned to each family for ongoing support. Funds from a special foundation, now closed for collection, will also aid victims and their families.

item.title: Kazakhstan mourns 14 soldiers lost in naval exercise tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan declared September 25 a day of mourning after 14 soldiers died during a naval exercise in the Caspian Sea. A sudden storm caused a boat carrying 17 soldiers to capsize, sweeping them away. Three soldiers were rescued. Criminal charges have been filed, and five officials are in custody.

item.title: Russia significantly increased diesel fuel supplies to Kyrgyzstan in August
item.description: In August, Russia supplied over 72,000 tons of diesel fuel to Kyrgyzstan, a substantial increase from the 4,400 tons delivered in July. Traders reported that this represents a more than 16-fold rise in monthly deliveries.
